objective.text: The investigation aimed to quantify the sizes of liquid smoke particulates in low gravity and relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions.
objective.quote: One of the major goals of this investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.

fuel.text: The smoke was generated by overheated spacecraft materials.
fuel.quote: The measurements were made using smoke generated by overheated  spacecraft materials where variables such as the sample temperature, flow field, and particle aging time were more rigorously controlled.

variables.text: Variables such as the sample temperature, flow field, and particle aging time were controlled.
variables.quote: where variables such as the sample temperature, flow field, and particle aging time were more rigorously controlled.

measurements.text: Primary and aggregate particle dimensions were determined using a Transmission Electron microscope.
measurements.quote: After flight, the particulate collected on the thermophoretic probes were analyzed using a Transmission Electron microscope (TEM) to determine primary and aggregate particle dimensions.

safety_finding.text: Changes in smoke size distribution and number density in microgravity can result in some detectors not producing an alarm.
safety_finding.quote: The change in the size distribution and number density will, in turn, affect the response of the smoke detectors and possibly result in some detectors not producing an alarm when exposed to this smoke.

earth_benefits.text: Smoke detectors developed from the results can be useful in extreme environments on Earth such as submarines or underwater laboratories.
earth_benefits.quote: The smoke detectors developed from the results of SAME can also be useful in other extreme environments on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories.
